key_insight: CAFM reframes EHR foundation models around patient cohorts as explicit clinical evidence, aiming to improve interpretability, robustness, and alignment with clinician reasoning.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this cohort-anchored approach could make AI outputs more auditable and clinically meaningful for risk prediction, triage, and report generation across modalities.
method: Deviation-aware data curation to improve cohort quality and reduce noisy comparisons
Cohort-conditioned pretraining plus multimodal cohort alignment to organize representations around clinically meaningful peer groups
Clinician-in-the-loop refinement to support auditable decision-making without changing underlying encoders
evidence_signal: The abstract presents four clinical case studies and five empirically testable hypotheses, but it does not report new performance results or external validation.
watch_item: The framework still needs careful evaluation under distribution shift and across irregular, multimodal EHR data before it can be considered reliable for deployment.
paper_title: Cohort-Anchored Foundation Models for Electronic Health Records: From Risk Scores to Auditable Peer Cohorts
